''''Ubadah ibn al-Samit''' ({{langx|ar|عُبَادَة بۡن ٱلصَّامِت}} {{transliteration|ar|ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit}}) was a [[companion of Muhammad]] and a well-respected chieftain of the [[Ansar (Islam)|Ansar]]. He participated in almost every battle during [[Muhammad]]'s era. His official title, according to Muslim scholarly tradition, was 'Ubadah ''ibn Saamit al-Ansari al-Badri'' ({{lang|ar|عُبَادَة بۡن ٱلصَّامِت ٱلۡأَنْصَارِيّ ٱلۡبَدْرِيّ}}) for his actions at the [[Battle of Badr]].<ref name="Badar al Kubra position" /> He served under the first three [[Rashidun]] caliphs in the Muslim campaigns against the [[Byzantine Empire]].

The conquest of [[Cyprus]] marked 'Ubadah as one of the [[Rashidun army]]'s most successful military commanders. He participated in more than seven large scale military campaigns before ending his career as a [[qadi]] in the [[Holy Land]]. In later years he assisted [[Mu'awiya I|Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan]], the governor of [[Bilad al-Sham|Syria]] and future founder of the [[Umayyad Caliphate]].

'Ubadah served as the Quranic teacher of the [[Suffah]], as well as the [[mufti]] and judge of the [[Rashidun Caliphate]], and was involved in the matters of converting subdued populations and building [[mosque]]s, such as the [[Amr ibn al-As Mosque]] in [[Egypt]] and the [[Congregational mosque]] in [[Homs]]. Despite his low structural position, 'Ubadah's influence as a respected senior sahaba who was trusted by Muhammad and Caliph [[Umar]] could over-rule many of his compatriots, including those who outranked him structurally such as [[Mu'awiya I|Mu'awiya]], who served as Governor of [[Homs]] during 'Ubadah's tenure as judge.{{Citation needed|date=September 2022}}

Islamic scholars regard 'Ubadah as an influential companion of Muhammad who passed down many [[hadiths]] that became the basis of [[fiqh]] ruling in various matters.<ref name="auto3">{{harvnb|Sulaymān ibn al-Ashʻath al-Sijistānī|1984 |p=1012}}</ref><ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" />

== Early life ==
'Ubadah was a descendant of [[Yemen]]i Arabs who settled in [[Yathrib]] and formed the [[Banu Aws]] and [[Banu Khazraj|Khazraj]] tribes. He was born into the latter and became a prominent chief.<ref name="Jerusalem: The Biography">{{harvnb|Sebag Montefore|2012|p=226}}</ref> His genealogical lineage was 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit Ibn Qais bin Asram bin Fahr bin Tha'labah ibn Ghanm ibn Auf ibn (Amr bin Auf) ibn Al Khazraj. Sometime before Muhammad's migration from [[Mecca]], 'Ubadah and other Banu Aws and Khazraj tribe chieftains, such as [[Abd Allah ibn Rawahah]], ʿAbdullah ibn Haram, [[Sa'd ibn Ubadah|Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah]], and [[Abu Talha al-Ansari]], met Muhammad at [[Aqabah]] during their journey from [[Medina]] to perform [[Hajj]] in [[Mecca]]. In historical literature, these clan leaders are said to have done Hajj to achieve enlightenment after they grew weary of tribal conflicts, particularly the civil war of Yathrib that Muslim historians call the [[Yawm al-Buath|Battle of Bu'ath]]. They listened to Muhammad's preaching and considered him to be the solution to unite their tribes. They immediately pledged their allegiance to him, marking this event as the first pledge of al-Aqabah. 'Ubadah was around forty years old.<ref name="sunnipath2">{{Citation | title = The Sealed Nectar | contribution-url = http://www.sunnipath.com/Resources/PrintMedia/Books/B0033P0017.aspx | contribution = The Second 'Aqabah Pledge | publisher = Sunni path| title-link = The Sealed Nectar }}</ref><ref name="representatives">{{Citation | title = Abd Allah ibn Rawaahah | url = http://www.islamic-council.org/lib/men/ABD-ALLAH-IBN-RAWAAHAH.html | publisher = Islamic council | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20060630073952/http://www.islamic-council.org/lib/men/ABD-ALLAH-IBN-RAWAAHAH.html | archive-date = 2006-06-30 }}</ref> Later he participated in the [[Second pledge at al-Aqabah]], and narrated the event.

{{cquote
| bgcolor = #F0FFF0|''I was among those who were present at Aqabah. We were twelve men who took an oath of allegiance to the Messenger of Allah Sallallahu Alayhi Wasallam in the Pledge of Aqabah, which was called Bai'at An-Nisa'{{#tag:ref|It was called Baiat an Nisa, or Pledge of the Women, because of the presence of 'Afra bint 'Ubaid ibn Tha'labah, who was the first women to swear an oath of allegiance<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mZmBkoDa9fcC&q=Ahmad+Ghadanfar+ubadah+samit|title=Atlas Al-sīrah Al-Nabawīyah|date=February 1, 2004|publisher=Darussalam|via=Google Books|isbn=978-9960-897-71-4}}</ref>|group="Notes"}} This was before the fighting was enjoined, so we pledged not to associate anything with Allah, not to steal, not to commit adultery, not to kill our children, not to intentionally forge falsehood,{{#tag:ref|Referencing [[Al-Mumtahanah]] verse 12|group="Notes"}} and not to disobey him in any just matter. "If you fulfil that then Paradise will be yours, but if you commit any of these sins, it is for Allah to forgive or punish as He wills'<ref name="Atlas Sirah Nabawiyah">{{cite book |last1=Abu Khalil |first1=Shawqī |title=Atlas Al-sīrah Al-Nabawīyah |date=2004 |publisher=Darussalam |isbn=9960-897-71-0 |page=292 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mZmBkoDa9fcC&q=Ahmad+Ghadanfar+ubadah+samit |access-date=30 January 2020}}</ref> "''
}}

When the [[Muhajirun|Meccan]] Muslims [[Hijrah|were migrating]] to seek refuge in Yathrib (now Medina), 'Ubadah and his fellow [[Banu Aws]] and [[Kharijites|Khazraji]] provided shelter to them as Muhammad immediately instructed 'Ubadah to take an oath of brotherhood with the [[Muhajirun]] named Abu Marthad al-Ghanwi.<ref name="Mahmud" />

=== Battles under Muhammad ===
{{Campaignbox Campaigns of Muhammad}}
During Muhammad's stay in Yathrib, 'Ubadah participated at the [[Battle of Badr]], which elevated his status as a patron of [[Islam]] in the view of Muslim scholars and earned him the title of ''al-Badri'', which is bestowed to Muslims who attended the battle.<ref name="Badar al Kubra position" /><ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> 'Ubadah gave his testimony in regards to the aftermath of the battle when the Muslim army discussed their prisoners of war.<ref name="Badar al Kubra position" />

'Ubadah also participated in the [[Battle of Uhud]].{{sfn|al-Dihlawī |1991|p=401}}

After the incident between the [[Banu Qaynuqa]] tribe and Muhammad, 'Ubadah announced that he had annulled the alliance with the Banu Qaynuqa, and it was this incident that led to the [[Waḥy|revelation]] of {{Quranverse|5|51|c=y}} and {{Quranverse|5|52|c=y}} from [[God in Islam|God]] to Muhammad. 'Ubadah's position as a respected head of the clan superseded [[Abd Allah ibn Ubayy]]'s (another Khazraji chief) support of the [[Jews]]. In the end, the entire clan instead followed 'Ubadah and supported Muhammad and they expelled the Banu Qaynuqa Jews from Medina and took their [[date palm]] gardens as a [[holy war]] benefit for the city's Muslim community before continuing to serve in the [[Battle of the Trench|Battle of Khandaq]].<ref name="auto4">{{harvnb|Gil|1997|p=119}}</ref> In January 627, the Ansaris under 'Ubadah and his colleague, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, led an expedition against the [[Banu Mustaliq]] tribe. The raid was successful and they took 200 families captive, along with 200 camels, 5,000 sheep, goats, and a large quantity of household goods.<ref name="TheSealed">{{citation |title=The Sealed Nectar: biography of the Noble Prophet |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r_80rJHIaOMC&pg=PA386 |first=Saifur Rahman Al |last=Mubarakpuri |year=2005 |publisher=Darussalam Publications |pages=386–387 |isbn=978-9960-899-55-8 }} ([http://www.witness-pioneer.org/vil/Books/SM_tsn/ch4s12.html online] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726140719/http://www.witness-pioneer.org/vil/Books/SM_tsn/ch4s12.html |date=2011-07-26 }})</ref> However, during the battle 'Ubadah unintentionally killed one of his Ansari clansmen, Hisham ibn Subabah.<ref name="(Ibn Hisham) part 3 p. 187.">{{cite web |last1=Ahmed Ali Abdel-Qader Muhammad al-Maqrizi |first1=Taqi al-Din |title=Battle with Banu Mustaliq |url=https://www.withprophet.com/ar/غزوة-بني-المصطلق_1382 |website=With prophet |access-date=30 January 2020}}</ref> Sometime after the [[Treaty of Hudaybiyya]], 'Ubadah fought in the [[Battle of Khaybar]].<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" />

'Ubadah participated in virtually all military expeditions personally led by Muhammad before his death.<ref name="auto4" />

== Rashidun Caliphate ==
{{Campaignbox Byzantine-Arab Wars}}
After the selection of the first caliph, rebellion broke out across the caliphate. 'Ubadah was commanded by Caliph Abu Bakr to quell the [[Ridda Wars|rebellions across Arabia]], though it is not recorded which battles he was involved in.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Basalamah  |first1=Dr. Khalid Abdullah Zeed |title=Seerah Abu Bakr session 3 public lecture |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9g-arPiOEjI&list=PLlK0gGuioshBxyBg4TzEtKETkzOfv4mvB&index=50  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211220/9g-arPiOEjI |archive-date=2021-12-20 |url-status=live|website=Youtube |date=21 December 2014 |publisher=Khalid Basalamah official |access-date=27 January 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Basalamah  |first1=Dr. Khalid Abdullah Zeed |title=Seerah Sa'd ibn Ubadah public lecture |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Etoerx_FUjI  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211220/Etoerx_FUjI |archive-date=2021-12-20 |url-status=live|website=Youtube |date=22 January 2020 |publisher=Khalid Basalamah official |access-date=27 January 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref> According to David Nicolle, the four Rashidun contingents left Medina between the autumn of 633 to 634 before Khalid converged with other contingents led by generals such as [[Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah]], [[Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan]], [[Amr ibn al-As]] and [[Shurahbil ibn Hasana]].<ref name="DN46">D. Nicolle, ''Yarmuk 636 AD – The Muslim Conquest of Syria'', Osprey, 1994, p. 46.</ref> 'Ubadah, [[Abu al-Darda]], and [[Muadh ibn Jabal]] were sent to [[Syria]] after the caliph was asked to send preachers to teach the newly subdued Syrian Christians. At some point, 'Ubadah was tasked to assist the military campaigns in Syria.<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /><ref name="Mahmud" />

During the time of Caliph [[Umar bin Khattab|Umar ibn al-Khattab]], reinforcement requests came from the Syrian front during the Rashidun's [[Muslim conquest of the Levant|conquest of Levant]]. Umar sent 'Ubadah to join forces with [[Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah|Abu Ubayda]] and [[Khalid ibn al-Walid]].<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> 'Ubadah participated in the [[Battle of Ajnadayn]] under Khalid ibn al-Walid, where the 100,000 Byzantine soldiers under General Vardan were trapped and defeated, and then fled to [[Damascus]]. This battle ended with more than half of the Byzantine army killed, including Vardan.<ref>{{harvnb|Gil|1997|p=1485}}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia | title = Ad̲j̲nādayn | first = H.A.R. | last = Gibb | author-link = H.A.R. Gibb | encyclopedia = The Encyclopedia of Islam, New Edition, Volume I: A–B | publisher = BRILL | location = Leiden and New York | year = 1986 | isbn = 90-04-08114-3 | page = 208 | url = http://referenceworks.brillonline.com/entries/encyclopaedia-of-islam-2/ad-j-na-dayn-SIM_0329 | ref=Waqidi; Futuhusham}}</ref>

During the [[Siege of Emesa]] between 635 and 636 AD, Abu Ubaydah appointed 'Ubadah as his deputy in Homs while Abu Ubaydah left to capture [[Hamah]]. 'Ubadah stayed there with his wife, [[Umm Haram]], where Umm Haram remembered the hadith that allegedly prophesied the future conquest of [[Cyprus]] in which she and her husband participated.<ref>{{cite book |last1=al-Quraibi |last2=Afkar |first1=Ibrahim |first2=Dahyal |title=Tarikh al-Khulafa |date=2016 |publisher=Qisthi press |isbn=978-979-1303-40-8 |page=502 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WMNzDQAAQBAJ&pg=PA630 |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref>

{| class="toccolours" style="float: left; margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 2em; font-size: 85%; background:#c6dbf7; color:black; width:30em; max-width: 40%;" cellspacing="5"
| style="text-align: left;" |''Oh Jabla. Don't you know how we faced your advanced forces at Ajnadain and other places and how Allah Subhanahu Wa ta 'Ala granted us victory over you and how your tyrant ran away? We know who remains from your forces and they are easy for us. We are not afraid of these forces that have come. We have tasted blood and we haven't found blood sweeter than the blood of the Romans! Jabla, I call you to the religion of Islam and to enter our religion with your people and keep your honor in this life and the next life. do not be a servant of these uncouth Romans and put your life on the line to save them from destruction. You are from the chiefs of the Arabs and a king. Verily our religion has appeared. Follow the path of those who have repented and returned to Allah and believe in Him and say: "There is no God but Allah and Mohamed is the Messenger of Allah…"''<ref name="auto1" />
|-
| style="text-align: left;" |''''Ubadah ibn al-Samit taunt to [[Jabalah ibn al-Aiham]] before the [[Battle of the Yarmuk|Battle of Yarmuk]]'''
|}

'Ubadah participated in the [[Battle of Yarmouk]].<ref name="auto1">{{cite book |last1=ibn ʻUmar Wāqidī |first1=Muḥammad |title=Futuhusham |date=2005 |publisher=Ta-ha |isbn=1-84200-067-5 |page=389 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qM0tAQAAIAAJ&q=ubadah+samit |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref>

After they defeated the Byzantine coalitions in Yarmouk, 'Ubadah, along with the army of Abu Ubaydah and Khalid, continued their conquest until they reached northern Syria, where they turned south to pacify coastal Levant. 'Ubadah was instructed to lead a detachment to subdue [[Tartus]], a coastal fortress city.<ref name="kitAb futuh al-buldAn; Baladhuri">{{cite web |last1=K. Hitti |first1=Phillip |title=The origins of the Islamic state: being a translation from the Arabic |url=https://archive.org/stream/originsofislamic01albauoft/originsofislamic01albauoft_djvu.txt |publisher=Columbia University |access-date=28 January 2020}}</ref> While 'Ubadah occupied Tartus in 636, Mu'awiya came to the city, and built an [[amsar]] complex, while also delegating fiefs to the garrison commanders.<ref name="Baladhuri" /><ref name="Al-Kāmil fī al-tārīkh">{{cite web |last1=Ibn Athir |first1=Ali |author-link1=Ali ibn al-Athir |title=Al-Kāmil fī al-tārīkh |trans-title="The Complete History"; |url=http://islamport.com/w/tkh/Web/331/424.htm |website=The comprehensive encyclopedia www.islamport.com |publisher=Al-Warraq website |access-date=26 November 2021 |archive-date=17 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220517095930/http://islamport.com/w/tkh/Web/331/424.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'Ubadah was commanded by Abu Ubaydah to march towards [[Jableh|Jablah]] and Laodicea ([[Latakia]]).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Taha al-Salmani |first1=Dr. Abdullah |title=ملخص البحث|url=https://www.philadelphia.edu.jo/arts/14th/papers/day_2/session_3/abdallah_salmani.doc |website=Philadelphia education |publisher=University of Mosul |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{cite book |last1=Baladhuri |first1=Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Jabir |title=The Origins of the Islamic State: Being a Translation from the Arabic Accompanied With Annotations, Geographic and Historic Notes of the Kitab Futuh Al-buldan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bcWtttJL3WEC&pg=PA216 |publisher=Cosimo, Inc |access-date=26 January 2020|isbn=978-1-61640-534-2 |date=March 2011 }}</ref><ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" />{{sfn|Schulze|1973|p=253}} 'Ubadah met with resistance from the local garrison during the [[Siege of Latakia (636)|siege of Latakia]]. He observed that the city had a massive gate that could only be opened by a large number of men. He ordered his men to camp and dig trenches that could hide a rider on horseback. 'Ubadah and his army pretended to return to Homs, while at night he ordered the army to return to hide themselves in the trench. When the people in Laodicea thought 'Ubadah had left, they opened the gate to let their cattle out. 'Ubadah then ordered his entire army to attack. The Byzantines were caught by surprise and failed to close the gate. He climbed the wall then gave the signal of [[takbir]] terrifying the Byzantines and causing them to flee towards Al-Yusaiyid.<ref name="Baladhuri">{{cite book |last1=Bin Yahya Bin Jabir Al Baladhuri |first1=Ahmad |last2=Hitti |first2=Phillip Kuri |title=The Origins of the Islamic State: Being a Translation from the Arabic Accompanied With Annotations, Geographic and Historic Notes of the Kitab Futuh Al-buldan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bcWtttJL3WEC&pg=PA237 |publisher=Cosimo |access-date=29 January 2020|isbn=978-1-61640-534-2 |date=March 2011 }}</ref> The fleeing Byzantine soldiers and local citizens returned and surrendered to 'Ubadah, who accepted their surrender and allowed them to return to their homes with specific conditions, including the obligation to pay the [[kharaj]] land tax.<ref name="Baladhuri" /> While 'Ubadah oversaw Latakia, no buildings were razed including churches, while starting to build mosques. He stayed to establish the order of the caliphate on the subdued population. One particular mosque, Jami' al Bazaar or Mosque al-Bazaar survives. Laodicea was renamed to Latakia or ''Al-Ladhiqiyah.''<ref name="kitAb futuh al-buldAn; Baladhuri" /><ref name="Futuh-ul-Balad(conquest of countries)">{{cite web |last1=al-Zibawi |first1=Mahmud |title=لاذقية العرب(Arabic Lattakia) |url=http://www.maaber.org/issue_september11/lookout1.htm |website=Maaber |access-date=28 January 2020}}</ref>

After settling matters in Latakia, 'Ubadah marched into other Byzantine controlled cities, and subdued them one by one from [[Salamiyah]] to the port city of [[Baniyas]].<ref name="Al-Kāmil fī al-tārīkh" />

Circa 630s, 'Ubadah subdued the city of [[Paltus]], which would become an Arab settlement called [[Arab al-Mulk]] during a later era, as recorded by [[Yaqut al-Hamawi]].{{sfn|le Strange|1890|page=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_ENANAAAAIAAJ/page/n542 493]|}}

=== Transfer to Egypt ===

In July 640, during the [[Siege of Babylon Fortress|siege of Babylon fortress]] in [[Egypt]] against the Byzantine forces, the caliph sent 'Ubadah with 4,000 soldiers.<ref name=":1">{{cite book |last1=Saleh |first1=Qasim a Ibrahim dan Muhammad A. |title=Buku Pintar Sejarah Islam |date=2014 |publisher=Serambi Ilmu Semesta |isbn=978-602-17919-5-0 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1s9nCwAAQBAJ&q=buku+pintar+sejarah+islam |language=id}}</ref> The four commanders were two veteran Muhajirun, [[Zubayr ibn al-Awwam]] and [[Miqdad ibn Aswad]]; a young Ansari commander named [[Maslama ibn Mukhallad]]; and 'Ubadah. These reinforcements arrived in September 640.<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> Imam [[Abd al-Rahman al-Awza'i|Awza'i]], a [[Tabi'un]] and founder of the now extinct Awza'i [[madhhab]], recorded that he witnessed the Muslim conquest of Egypt and confirmed that 'Ubadah was among the leaders.<ref name="الإصابة1" /> Amr ibn al-As decided to battle on the open field near [[Heliopolis (ancient Egypt)|Heliopolis]] in early to mid July 640. His 8,000 soldiers were led by Zubayr, 'Ubadah, Maslama, Miqdad, and [[Kharija ibn Hudhafa]]. They defeated the 20,000 strong Byzantine army under Theodore.<ref name="Al-Dahabi Egypt">{{cite web |last1=Siyar A'lam Nubala |first1=Ibn Dhahabi |title=عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه داهية العرب.. فاتح مصر |url=https://www.lahaonline.com/articles/view/41721.htm |website=ـ موقع الشيخ حمد الحقيل |publisher=Laha Online |access-date=30 January 2020 |archive-date=10 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220310004020/https://www.lahaonline.com/articles/view/41721.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="HassonEI3">{{cite encyclopedia |last=Hasson |first=Isaac |article=Busr b. Abī Arṭāt |encyclopedia=Encyclopaedia of Islam |editor1=Fleet, Kate |editor2=Krämer, Gudrun |editor3=Matringe, Denis |editor4=Nawas, John |editor5=Rowson, Everett |year=2019 |orig-date=2011 |url=https://referenceworks.brillonline.com/entries/encyclopaedia-of-islam-3/busr-b-abi-artat-COM_24369?s.num=82&s.start=80}}</ref> The Muslims besieged the fortress over the course of months without a clear victory. During the siege, both sides exchanged envoys in an effort to demoralize each other.<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> In the days leading up to the end, 'Ubadah was sent with a delegation to [[Muqawqis]] to negotiate for the last time. It is said that Muqawqis became afraid of 'Ubadah when he saw 'Ubadah's dark and majestic appearance. 'Ubadah then mocked Muqawqis in a chronicle:

{{Blockquote|text=''Truly there are 1,000 of my comrades behind me. They are peoples who have darker skin than me and more sinister than me. if you saw them you would be more scared than you see me. I was appointed (as the leader) and my youth had passed. and praise be to Allah. You know, I'm not afraid if 100 of your people face me alone at once. so are my comrades behind me''<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" />|author=|title=|source=}}

'Ubadah gave him three options: accept Islam, pay ''[[jizyah]]'', or fight.<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> Following the failed negotiation, Byzantine forces decided to fight, and on the same day the fortress fell to the Muslims led [[Zubayr ibn al-Awwam]] who climbed the fortress wall alone and opened the gate from inside.<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> After the fortress had been taken, al-Aas consulted with [[Maslama ibn Mukhallad]]. Maslama suggested that Amr give a field command to 'Ubadah to attack [[Alexandria]]. 'Ubadah rode to Amr, who gave him his spear of command.<ref name="Ibnu Abdul Hakam; Futuh Mishri wa Akhbaruha" /> 'Ubadah rode towards the army and gave a speech before commencing his [[Siege of Alexandria (641)|attack on Alexandria]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Penaklukan Mesir Dan Alexandria; Bab III |url=http://digilib.uinsby.ac.id/18259/6/Bab%203.pdf |website=digital library |access-date=28 January 2020 |archive-date=31 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200331143144/http://digilib.uinsby.ac.id/18259/6/Bab%203.pdf }}</ref> 'Ubadah led a detachment to besiege Alexandria and reused his strategy of using trenches as he had with Latakia. When he and his main force arrived at Alexandria's outskirts, he gave a signal to the army including those hidden in the trenches to launch an assault. His attack breached and routed the Alexandrian forces on the first charge.<ref name="Mahmud">{{cite book |last1=Ahmad Ghadanfar |first1=Mahmood |last2=Al-Khaiat |first2=Abdul-Latif |title=The Commanders of Muslim Army |date=2001 |publisher=Darussalam Publishers |page=392 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TmWTBQAAQBAJ&pg=PT210 |access-date=28 January 2020}}</ref> After Alexandria, 'Ubadah stayed in Egypt to help Amr build the city of [[Fustat]] and its landmark, the Mosque of Amr ibn al-As.

=== Return to the Levant ===
'Ubadah was dispatched by Caliph [[Umar]] to assist Abu Ubaydah and Mu'awiya in Syria. Until the last years of his life, Umar wanted to appoint 'Ubadah as governor in Homs, as he thought that the grip of the caliphate and Islam was new in that area, so he wanted someone he trusted to impose strict order.<ref name="auto4" /> 'Ubadah declined the offer and then agreed to be instead appointed as [[qadi]] in Palestine. 'Ubadah spent time during his tenure as qadi to teach the Quran and hadiths, opened a public [[Majlis]]<ref name="auto4" /> and led sermons.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sayyid |first1=Kamali |title=رجل بألف رجل |url=https://maktubes.com/عبادة-بن-الصامت-رضي-الله-عنه/ |website=maktubes |date=19 October 2019 |access-date=27 January 2020 }}</ref><ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> 'Ubadah joined the main force of Mu'awiya to conquer [[Caesarea Maritima|Caesarea]] in 640 and was appointed to lead the right flank of the Mu'awiya corps during the last battle against the [[Ancient Rome|Romans]] at Qaysariyyah or [[Caesarea Maritima]], The Muslims were repelled several times before 'Ubadah and his men crushed the Byzantine ranks in a single charge that broke the stalemate. This allowed the Muslim forces to annex the historical territory of Byzantine, which led to the formation of the [[Jund Filistin]]. This ended 'Ubadah's journey in the Levant. During this time, 'Ubadah was appointed as the first governor of Jund Filistin.<ref name="Salmani Taha">{{cite web |last1=Taha al-Salmani |first1=Dr. Abdullah |title=ملخص البحث |url=https://www.philadelphia.edu.jo/arts/14th/papers/day_2/session_3/abdallah_salmani.doc |website=Philadelphia education |publisher=University of Mosul |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="auto" /><ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> Later, 'Ubadah assisted [[Mu'awiya]] to attack [[Amorium]], 170 miles southeast of [[Constantinople]],<ref name="History of Tabari">{{cite book |last1=Ibn Jarir at-Tabari |first1=Muhammad|author-link1=Tabari |title=The History of Al-Tabari Vol. 14: The Conquest of Iran A.D. 641-643/A.H. 21-23 |date=2015 |publisher=State University of New York Press |isbn=978-1-4384-2039-4 |page=164 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fRjsrA5tfLIC |access-date=25 November 2021 |language=en|translator=G. Rex Smith |format=Ebook}}</ref> in the winter of 644 with a force of 10,000 men.<ref name="Hepi Andi bastoni">{{cite book |last1=Andi Bastoni |first1=Hepi |title=Wajah Politik Muawiyah Bin Abu Sufyan: Mengurai Sejarah Konflik Sunni-Syiah |date=2012 |publisher=Pustaka Bustan |isbn=978-979-1324-07-6 |page=29 |edition=Original |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mCltDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA29 |access-date=7 February 2020}}</ref> This raiding operation started from area called Shaifa and ended in Amorium.<ref name="Hepi Andi bastoni" />

=== First Conquest of Cyprus ===
[[File:Atlas Van der Hagen-KW1049B13 007-CYPRVS INSVLA.jpeg|thumb|The middle age depiction of Cyprus, where 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit under Muawiyah conquered]]

Some-time during the [[Muslim conquest of the Levant]], Mu'awiya asked Umar to allow him to build a navy which he would command to conquer the island of [[Cyprus]]. However, Umar felt hesitant to give permission and he instead asked the other Rashidun commanders 'Ubadah, Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-As. Amr expressed his doubts that the Rashidun army was ready to mount such naval operations, which prompted Umar to duly reject the proposal of Mu'awiya.<ref name="الكامل في التاريخ">{{cite book |author1=Ibn al-Athir |author1-link=Ibn al-Athir |editor1-last=Al-Qadi |editor1-first=Abu Al-Fida Abdullah |title=الكامل في التاريخ |volume=2 |date=1987 |publisher=الكتب العلمية |page=488 |url=https://waqfeya.net/book.php?bid=1106 |access-date=20 April 2024 |language=Ar}}</ref><ref name="تاريخ الطبري (تاريخ الأمم والملوك) 1-6 مع الفهارس ج2">{{cite book |author1=Al-Tabari |author1-link=Al-Tabari |title=تاريخ الطبري (تاريخ الأمم والملوك) 1-6 مع الفهارس ج2 |date=2011 |publisher=Dar Al Kotob Al Ilmiya |page=900 |access-date=20 April 2024 |language=Ar|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6cdwDwAAQBAJ}}</ref> When [[Uthman]] became caliph after Umar's death, Mu'awiya once again asked the Caliph to allow him to build a navy to attack Cyprus, reasoning that Cyprus had become a satellite island of Byzantine forces which could threaten the caliphate on the western banks of Palestine.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" />

'Ubadah, along with veteran companions of Muhammad such as Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, [[Abu Dharr al-Ghifari]], [[Shaddad ibn Aws]], Khalid bin Zayd al-Ansari, and [[Abu Ayyub al-Ansari]], all participated in building the caliphate's first naval armada, led by Mu'awiya.<ref name="Legenda 4 Umara">{{cite book |last1=Indra |first1=Gunawan |title=Legenda 4 Umara Besar |publisher=Elex Media Komputindo |isbn=978-602-02-3477-9 |page=280 |date=2014-03-13 }}</ref><ref name="Ibn Hajjar, Tahdhib, V, III ff">{{cite book |last1=Rex |first1=Smith |title=The History of al-Tabari Vol. 14: The Conquest of Iran A.D. 641-643/A.H. 21-23 |date=2015 |isbn=978-1-4384-2039-4 |page=164 |publisher=State University of New York Press }}</ref> Before he joined Mu'awiya's project to build the first naval forces of the caliphate, 'Ubadah joined forces with Muslim general, [[Abdallah ibn Qais]].<ref name="Humphrey">{{cite book |last1=Humphrey |first1=R. Stephen |author2=Muhammad Tabari |editor1-last=Humphrey |editor1-first=Stephen |title=The History of al-Tabari Vol. 15: The Crisis of the Early Caliphate: The Reign of 'Uthman A.D. 644-656/A.H. 24-35 |publisher=SUNY press |isbn=978-0-7914-0154-5 |page=285 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oALIyvjV0fEC&pg=PA25|date=January 1990 }}</ref> Shortly after building the armada, Mu'awiya and 'Ubadah departed from [[Acre, Israel|Acre]] and left for [[Cyprus]].<ref name="auto2">{{cite book |author=Al Ghazali |title=Muawiyah – Sebuah Biografi Awal |date=2015 |publisher=PTS Publications & Distributors Sdn Bhd |isbn=978-967-411-446-6 |page=176 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uT_DCgAAQBAJ&pg=PT65 |access-date=26 January 2020}}</ref> According to [[al-Baladhuri]] and [[Khalifa ibn Khayyat]], Mu'awiya and 'Ubadah led the attack and were accompanied by their wives Katwa bint Qaraza ibn Abd Amr of the Qurayshite [[Banu Nawfal]] and Umm Haram.<ref name="Sahih al-Bukhari 2788" /> Umm Haram died in an accident during the campaign.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" /> The Muslim forces accepted Cyprus's surrender under the condition that they refrain from hostility to Muslims, inform the Caliphate of any Byzantine movements, pay 7,200 dinars annually as the [[jizya]], and never reveal information to outsiders regarding the caliphate's military operations.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" />

Mu'awiya and 'Ubadah's forces pacified almost every Byzantine garrison. This is evidenced by two Greek inscriptions in the Cypriot village of Solois that note those two offensives.{{sfn|Lynch|2016|p=539}} The entire island of Cyprus surrendered after their capital, [[Salamis, Cyprus|Salamis]], was surrounded and besieged.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" /> At least 50 military operations occurred in Cyprus between this first campaign carried out in 648 until the last one in 650.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]">{{cite book |last1=Sallabi |first1=Ali Muhammad |title=Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan |date=2007 |publisher=مكتبة العصيرية |isbn=978-9953-34-717-2 |page=654 |edition=original |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=a0YDzQEACAAJ |access-date=3 February 2020|author1-link=Ali al-Sallabi }}</ref>

One of the most famous hadiths related to 'Ubadah and Umm Haram relate to the prophecy that the Islamic caliphate would dominate the sea on two occasions. This was taught by Muslim scholars as a prophecy of the conquest of Cyprus.<ref name="Sahih al-Bukhari 2788" /> 'Ubadah participated in both the initial conquest and the second campaign years later. Umm Haram narrated the prophecy, which she believed related to this campaign. [[Anas ibn Malik]], her nephew, reminded them about then hadith of the promise of incoming naval conquests by Islam.<ref name="Sahih al-Bukhari 2788" />

=== Second Conquest of Cyprus ===
{{Further|Cyprus in the Middle Ages}}
In 652, Cyprus rebelled against the caliphate, causing Mu'awiya and 'Ubadah to mount a second campaign.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" /> This time Mu'awiya and 'Ubadah split their forces: one led by Mu'awiya and the other by [[Abd Allah ibn Sa'd]]. This punitive campaign was described in Tarikh fi Asr al-Khulafa ar-Rashidin as particularly ruthless. Many died in the campaign and many were taken captive.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" />

After they pacified Cyprus, 'Ubadah told Mu'awiya to divide the spoils in fifths according to the [[Sunnah|teachings of Muhammad]].<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" /> Mu'awiya agreed with 'Ubadah's counsel and gave him the task. Afterwards, Mu'awiya consulted with one of his officers, Ismail ibn al-Ayyash, as to how to prevent another uprising. Then Mu'awiya posted a garrison of 12,000 soldiers. Mu'awiya also transferred Muslim settlers from [[Baalbek]] to Cyprus and constructed mosques there.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" />

== Later life and death ==
[[File:Muslim Cemetery Eastern Wall Jerusalem 14.jpg|thumb|Entrance to the [[Bāb ar-Raḥma Cemetery]], Jerusalem, where the grave of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit located.]]
At the end of his military career, 'Ubadah retired to Palestine. When Caliph [[Uthman]] faced increasing opposition to his authority, 'Ubadah was among those who expressed support for him and opposed the revolts against Uthman's rule.<ref name="Mirza-Dissension">{{cite book |last1=Bashir-ud-Din Mahmud Ahmad |first1=Mirza |title=The Outset of Dissension in Islam |date=June 1, 2013|publisher=Islam International Publications Ltd |isbn=978-1-84880-092-2 |page=167 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1LC9DwAAQBAJ&pg=PA68 |access-date=30 January 2020}}</ref> He, Mu'awiya, [[Kharija ibn Hudhafa]] of Egypt, Anas ibn Malik, Hisham ibn Amir, Abu Darda, and [[Tabi'un|Tabiin]] pupils of [[Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud]] were among those from outside Medina who urged the caliphate to take action against the dissidents in Medina.<ref name="Humphrey" />

'Ubadah died in [[Ramla]] at the age of 72.<ref name="Abu Yusuf, 81; Ibn Asakir, VII, 210f">{{harvnb|Gil|1997|p=135}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wCVIZIIvMSkC&pg=PA21|title=Hak dan Batil dalam pertentangan|last=Abbah|first=Ibrahim Abu|date=1997|publisher=Gema Insani|isbn=978-979-561-444-9|language=id}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ASaPAAAAMAAJ&q=34+AH|title=The Men of Madina|last=Saʻd|first=Muḥammad Ibn|date=1997|publisher=Ta-Ha Publishers|isbn=978-1-897940-68-6|language=en}}</ref> 'Ubadah said on his deathbed:

{{Blockquote|text=By Allah, every Hadith (from the Prophet) which I heard from Rasulullah Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam. I will tell you because not long time before i leave this world, i will tell one Hadith. I have heard that Rasulullah Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam has said:

''"Whoever testifies to that there is no God besides Allah and Prophet Muhammad is messenger of Allah, then Allah will forbid the hellfire to (burn) him"'' {{#tag:ref|Sahih Muslim (29) al-Iman <ref>{{cite book |last1=Abu Abbah |first1=Ibrahim |title=Hak dan Batil dalam pertentangan |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wCVIZIIvMSkC&q=%27ubadah+shamit |publisher=Gema Insani, 2017 |access-date=31 January 2020|isbn=978-979-561-444-9 |year=1997 }}</ref>}}|author=|title=|source=}}

== Personal information ==
=== Appearance ===
Ibn Hajar in his ''Siyar A'lam Nubala'' in the chapter of 'Ubadah describes him as physically attractive.<ref name="Siyar a'lam Nubala" /> Several historians said his enemies were awed by his appearance.<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" />

=== Family ===
'Ubadah's sister was named Nusaybah.<ref name="Jerusalem: The Biography" /> His father was Samit Ibn Qais Ibn Asram Ibn Fahr while his mother was Qarat al-Ain Bint 'Ubadah bin Nidhal al-Khazrajiyya. His brother, 'Aws bin al-Samit, was married to [[Khawla bint Tha'labah]], a disciple ([[Companions of the Prophet|Sahaba]]) of Muhammad who was mentioned in Sura [[Al-Mujadila]].

Records from [[Sahih al-Bukhari]] and [[Sahih Muslim]] included a statement from Anas ibn Malik that 'Ubadah was married to Umm Haram bint Milhan during the first conquest of Cyprus with Mu'awiya, who died during the campaign. [[Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani]] translated this to mean 'Ubadah married Umm Haram during the campaign. However, [[Ibn Ishaq]] disagreed and translated the words of Anas to mean Umm Haram had married 'Ubadah before the campaign. Ibn Hajar argued further that another record from [[Ibn Hibban]] that stated that Umm Haram had just married 'Ubadah, which caused Ibrahim al Quraibi, author of Tarikh ul-Khulafa, to support the opinion of Ibn Hajar.<ref name="Tarikh-Khulafa">{{cite book |last1=al Quraibi |first1=Ibrahim |last2=Askar Lc. |first2=Dahya |title=Tarikh Khulafa |date=2016 |publisher=Qisthi press |isbn=978-979-1303-40-8 |page=630 }}</ref>

'Ubadah was also married to Jamilah bint Abi Sa'sa' and they had a son named Walid ibn 'Ubadah.<ref name="الإصابة1" />

His son, Ubaydah ibn Ubadah ibn Ubadah, was buried in Egypt.<ref>{{cite news |last1=الشيمي |first1=علي شفيق |title="بقيع مصر الثاني".. "بهنسا" مدينة الشهداء |url=http://gate.ahram.org.eg/News/2243232.aspx |access-date=30 January 2020 |agency=Ahram |date=14 July 2019}}</ref>

=== Character ===
During his lifetime, 'Ubadah held influence within the caliphate's administration. He was asked to pass judgements, which only a handful of Muhammad's companions were allowed during their life.<ref name="Basic Concept of Sharia">{{cite book |last1=bin Mat Saad |first1=Hasbollah |title=THE BASIC CONCEPTS OF SHARIA |date=May 7, 2020 |publisher=PENA HIJRAH RESOURCES |isbn=978-967-5523-16-8 |pages=205, 372 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fozhDwAAQBAJ |access-date=14 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="Jurisprudence History">{{cite book |last1=Ali as-Sayiss |first1=Muhammad |last2=Touqan |first2=Rami |title=History of Islamic Jurisprudence |date=2016 |publisher=Dar Al Kotob Al Ilmiyah دار الكتب العلمية |isbn=978-2-7451-8248-7 |pages=169, 304 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AVBiDwAAQBAJ |access-date=14 October 2021}}</ref>

Regarding his battlefield achievements, 'Ubadah was known as a fearless warrior. Caliph Umar himself praised him as equal to 1,000 warriors.<ref name="Numbers and Mathematical Concepts in Islam">{{cite book |last1=Moradhun |first1=Teebaye |title=Numbers and Mathematical Concepts in Islam |publisher=Maths Concepts in Islam |page=83 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uaY1ONfU_pgC |access-date=28 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref> He was once recorded for displaying his personal military prowess when the Muslims had besieged a Byzantine fort. 'Ubadah was found alone praying in a field by Byzantine soldiers. Before they could approach, he jumped to his horse and advanced towards them. The Byzantine soldiers fled and were chased by 'Ubadah until they reached their fort.<ref name="Ibnu Abdul Hakam; Futuh Mishri wa Akhbaruha">{{cite book |author=Mahmud Musthofa Saad |author2=Nashir Abu Amir Al-Humaidi |title=Golden Stories: Kisah-kisah Indah dalam Sejarah Islam |date=2017 |publisher=Pustaka AL-Kautsar |isbn=978-979-592-643-6 |page=444 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pktmDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA443 |access-date=26 January 2020}}</ref>

He was known as a clever commander who deployed successful strategies, such as the use of ambush trenches which allowed him to conquer strongholds such as Latakia in Syria and Alexandria in Egypt.

Muslim historians described 'Ubadah as a proud man who could not be easily intimidated during negotiation. He is known as a solemn personality who detested sycophants, which he showed at one Friday prayer in Damascus. The [[khatib]] lauded him with praise when 'Ubadah was a chief judge. He threw mud in the Khatib's face and quoted the hadith about the instruction from Muhammad to throw mud in the face of flatterers.<ref name="Ghadanfar" /> Caliph Umar held 'Ubadah in high regard. The Caliph respected him to the extent that he gave 'Ubadah important tasks.<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> Caliph Umar supported 'Ubadah when the latter came into dispute with Mu'awiya. The caliph appointed 'Ubadah as a judge while giving him autonomy so that Mu'awiya, who was the governor of Syria, could not interfere with his verdicts.<ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> The source of the dispute was recorded by a hadith that was graded highly by [[Sunan ibn Majah]]. The hadith explained the difference between 'Ubadah and Mu'awiya regarding the permissibility of transactions using gold to exchange with coin of Dinar and silver with coin of Dirham.<ref name="Chapter: Venerating the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (saws) and dealing harshly with those who Oppose It" />

Sunni scholars classified 'Ubadah as among the higher-ranked companions of Muhammad.<ref name="caliphtv">{{cite web |url=http://www.caliphtv.com/files/khalid.bin.waleed/khalid/companions.html |title=Twelve Ranks of the Companions |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110423065308/http://www.caliphtv.com/files/khalid.bin.waleed/khalid/companions.html#12ranks |archive-date=2011-04-23}}</ref><ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" /> At least five reasons are stated by scholars that ranked 'Ubadah in such saintly venerable status according to the traditions of Islamic scholars:

* His participation in the Battle of Badr, which inaugurated the honorific title of ''"Al-Badri"''.{{sfn|al-Dihlawī |1991|p=401}} His status as a veteran is special in the eyes of scholars as Muhammad regarded those of his companions who attended the Battle of Badr as among the most important in Islam.<ref name="Badar al Kubra position">{{cite web |title=Badar al-Kubra, dispute regarding prisoners of war |date=8 November 2007 |url=http://midad.com/article/203159/غزوة-بدر-الكبرى-الخلاف-في-الأنفال-والأسرى |access-date=30 January 2020 |ref=Professor Muhammad al-Amin al-Masri}}</ref>

==== Jihad and laws of war ====
'Ubadah passed down Hadith that ruled the administration of [[Prize of war|Spoils of War]] such as the one after they pacified Cyprus for the second time. 'Ubadah told Mu'awiya to share the spoils that were acquired through military campaigns according to the [[Sunnah]], which must be divided in fifths.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" /> In response Mu'awiya tasked 'Ubadah to manage the spoils.<ref name="[[Ali al-Sallabi|Ali Sallabi]]" />

On smaller scale operations, such as limited military raids, a hadith says 'Ubadah said that Muhammad "awarded one quarter of the spoils to those who attacked the enemy at the beginning and one third to those who attacked at the end".<ref name="The Chapters on Jihad Chapter: Awards granted from the spoils of war">{{cite web |last1=ibn Yazīd Ibn Mājah al-Rabʻī al-Qazwīnī |first1=Muḥammad|author-link1= Ibn Majah |title=The Chapters on Jihad Chapter: Awards granted from the spoils of war |url=https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:2852 |access-date=26 November 2021 |ref=Book 24, Hadith 100 |quote=Sunan Ibn Majah 2852; graded as Sahih (authentic)}}</ref><ref name="Al-Sindi's Commentary on Ibn Majah » Jihad Book » Bab Al Nafl" /> Hanafi scholar [[Muhammad 'Abid al-Sindi]] preserved the exegesis from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Shaddad, that this Hadith rules that those involved in the start of the fight have right of one quarter of the spoils, while those who participated later acquired one third of the spoils.<ref name="Al-Sindi's Commentary on Ibn Majah » Jihad Book » Bab Al Nafl">{{cite web |last1=al-Sindi |first1=Muhammad 'Abid |author-link1=Muhammad 'Abid al-Sindi |title=Al-Sindi's Commentary on Ibn Majah » Jihad Book » Bab Al Nafl |url=https://islamweb.net/ar/library/index.php?page=bookcontents&ID=5294&bk_no=54&flag=1 |website=Islamweb |publisher=Islamweb Network |access-date=26 November 2021}}</ref>

Учебное Пособие Для Вузов |date=2021 |publisher=ЛитРес |isbn=978-5-04-071651-7 |page=156 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xDgkEAAAQBAJ |access-date=26 November 2021 |language=en|format=Ebook}}</ref><ref name="Qur'an, Hadith and Riba Connotation">{{cite journal |last1=Ayyub |first1=Muhammad |title=Qur'an, Hadith and Riba Connotation |journal=Journal of Islamic Business and Management |date=December 2012 |volume=2 |issue=2 |pages=59–98 |url=https://jibm.org/archieves/volume2-issue2/volume2-issue2-article3/ |doi=10.12816/0004982 |access-date=26 November 2021 |doi-access=free |archive-date=7 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220207160353/https://jibm.org/archieves/volume2-issue2/volume2-issue2-article3/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Haram Wealth in Contemporary Muamalah">{{cite book |last1=Tarmizi |first1=Erwandi |title=Haram Wealth in Contemporary Muamalah |date=2017 |publisher=PT Erwandi Tarmizi Konsultan |page=325 |isbn=978-602-19742-0-9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ylRhDgAAQBAJ |access-date=26 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Riba in Hadith">{{cite web |last1=Imran Ashraf Usmani |first1=Muhammad |title=Riba in Hadith |url=https://islamicmarkets.com/education/riba-in-hadith |website=Islamic Market |publisher=Meezan Bank's Guide to Islamic Banking. |access-date=26 November 2021 |archive-date=26 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211126050012/https://islamicmarkets.com/education/riba-in-hadith |url-status=dead }}</ref> It rules out hand-to-hand transactions of commodities. It requires that only similar items be traded, except where the transaction consisted of two different commodities.<ref name="Riba in Hadith" /> The exegete scholars agreed that this tradition from 'Ubadah covered at least one of the six types of ''riba'', ''Riba al Fadhl'' type, which rules that an increase in one of the two exchanged ribawi items that are of the same nature and type.<ref name="An Explanation of Rationale behind the Prohibition of Riba in the Doctrines of three major Religions : with special reference to Islam 利用統計を見る" /> Thus, on the scope of Madhhab schools, four major Madhhabs, along with [[Zahiri]], unanimously agreed on the implementation of bans for such types of ''Riba''. Although the degree of the ban differs among those Madhhabs, such as that Hanbalis disagreed with Hanafis' total ban for any items, as Hanbalis argues on the basis of [[Said ibn al-Musayyib]] reasoning, that the Hadith of 'Ubadah were limited to foodstuffs, as non-consumable items were exempted. Sa'ib used another authentic Hadith from [[Abu Sa'id al-Khudri]] to regard this matter as counterargument.<ref name="History of Usury Pohibition-EP-2: Causes of Riba in Four Major Schools of Islamic Jurisprudence.">{{cite document |last1=Ahmed Qureshi |first1=Fahad |title=History of Usury Pohibition-EP-2: Causes of Riba in Four Major Schools of Islamic Jurisprudence |publisher=Chief Coordinator – AAOIFI CSAA Program at TAIF Digital Institute for Islamic Finance |language=en|date=2016}}</ref>

Historical usage of this Hadith from 'Ubadah was found, as 'Ubadah tried to implemented the Hadith during the campaign of Cyprus.<ref name="Philosophy for Professionals. A Short Series of Practice-orientated Lectures and Reader" /> However, [[Sunan ibn Majah]] recorded that during his tenure as judge in Homs, this effort of 'Ubadah to implement the rule became the source of a dispute between 'Ubadah and city governor Mu'awiya.<ref name="Chapter: Venerating the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (saws) and dealing harshly with those who Oppose It" /> 'Ubadah argued by basing his argument from this Hadith of usury that Islam forbid the unequal exchanging of goods unless they were of similar quality, in this case the exchange of gold to with dinar and dirham. 'Ubadah viewed that it falls under a practice of ''Riba'', while Mu'awiya argued that there was no element of usury, except given delays in a transaction.<ref name="Chapter: Venerating the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (saws) and dealing harshly with those who Oppose It">{{cite web |last1=Ibn Majah |first1=Abū ʻAbdillāh Muḥammad ibn Yazīd |title=The Book of the Sunnah (2) Chapter: Venerating the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (saws) and dealing harshly with those who Oppose It |url=https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:18 |website=sunnah.com |publisher=Darussalam |access-date=22 September 2021}}</ref>{{#tag:ref|This report of dispute between Ubadah with Mu'awiyah were supported by record of [[Al-Nasa'i]]<ref name="44 The Book of Financial Transactions (44) Chapter: Selling Barley For Barley">{{cite web |last1=al-Nasā'ī |first1=Aḥmad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Alī ibn Sīnān |title=44 The Book of Financial Transactions (44) Chapter: Selling Barley For Barley |url=https://sunnah.com/nasai:4566 |website=Sunnah.com |access-date=26 November 2021 |ref=Darussalam Publisher |quote=It was narrated that 'Ubadah bin As-Samit said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah say: 'Gold, equal amount."' (One of the narrators) Yaqub did not mention: "Equal amount." Muawiyah said: "This does not mean anything." 'Ubadah said; "By Allah I do not care if I am in a land where Muawiyah is not present. I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah say that."}}</ref>|group="Notes"}} This Hadith was enough to overrule the early verdict regarding ''Riba'' by [[Ibn Abbas]], another companion of the Muhammad with similarly high rank. Previously Ibn Abbas gave a less strict verdict regarding ''Riba'', thus in the end Ubadah's ruling regarding Riba or Usury prevailed in opinions from majority of their peers, and caused Ibn Abbas to withdraw his previous rulings.<ref name="The Reason Why the Companion Ibn Abbas Changed His Opinion on Riba Al-fadhl; Ibn Abbas">{{cite journal |author1=Ibrahim Nuhu Tahir |title=The Reason Why the Companion Ibn Abbas Changed His Opinion on Riba Al-fadhl |journal=International Journal of Social Science and Humanity |date=2016 |volume=6 |issue=6 |pages=476–477 |url=https://www.ijssh.net/index.php?m=content&c=index&a=show&catid=76&id=1034 |access-date=24 April 2024 |language=En |issn=2010-3646}}</ref>

=== Architecture ===
[[File:جامع البازار في اللاذقية 8.JPG|thumb|Jami' al-Bazaar mosque in [[Latakia]] built by 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit during conquest of Levant]]
'Ubadah demonstrated his skill as an architect after the conquest of Latakia. While he administered the city, he built the Great Mosque of al-Bazaar. The mosque has two western entrances. South of the mosque, leading to its courtyard is an open space recently roofed with raspberry boards. From the eastern side, two spaces open in front of the mosque, a rectangle covered with six stone arches, and a medium-sized [[minaret]] stands on its highest base. The mosque does not contain artistic touches except for some decorations on the entrance and the minaret. On the western side of the mosque is an old bathroom.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Yusuf |first1=Ghazwan |title=Al-Bazaar mosque... 'Ubadah bin Samit lay it first foundation |url=http://www.esyria.sy/elatakia/index.php?p=stories&category=places&filename=200904021320011 |website=02 April 2009 Esyria |access-date=28 January 2020}}</ref>

Another example of his architecture is when he ended the conquest in Egypt with al-Aas. He was involved in planning and developing [[Fustat]] and in constructing the first mosque in Egypt, known as the [[Mosque of Amr ibn al-As|mosque of Amr bin al-As]]. He, along with other companions such as Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, Abu Darda, and Miqdad ibn Amr al-Aswad, also constructed and decided the [[Qibla]] or direction of prayer of the mosque.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ajeng Tedjomukti |first1=Ratna |title=Masjid Amru Bin Ash Tempat Sujud Pertama di Afrika; 07 Okt 2019 |url=https://khazanah.republika.co.id/berita/pyzxwl313/masjid-amru-bin-ash-tempat-sujud-pertama-di-afrika |website=Khazanah Republika |date=7 October 2019 |publisher=Republika press |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="Biografi Sirah Shahaba Nabi – Mahmud Al- Misri; Mukhtasar Seerat Ar-Rasul Ibn Hisham" />

=== Descendants and social developments ===
'Ubadah is revered by many [[Palestinian Arab]] communities who preserve his tomb in Ramla. Historical book author [[Simon Sebag Montefiore]] wrote that the keeper of 'Ubadah's tomb hails from the [[Nusaybah family]], a modern Arabic family that claims to be descendants of 'Ubadah and Nusaybah, his sister.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Sebag Montefiore |first1=Simon |title=Jerusalem: The Biography |date=Jan 2, 2012 |publisher=Pustaka Alvabet |isbn=978-602-9193-02-2 |page=226 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Vy-SCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA226 |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref> The Palestinian Arabs regard him as an influential figure as evidenced by the public sermon by Dr. Yusuf Juma Salama, one of the official khattib of [[Qibli Mosque|Al-Aqsa Mosque]] who spoke of 'Ubadah as the first judge of Palestine.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Salama |first1=Yusuf |title=عبادة بن الصامت أول قاض ٍبالإسلام في بيت المقدس |url=https://www.alittihad.ae/article/23911/2012/عبادة-بن-الصامت-أول-قاض-بالإسلام-في-بيت-المقدس |website=Al itihad |date=8 March 2012 |access-date=28 January 2020}}</ref> A notable descendant was [[Sari Nusseibeh]], a [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] Professor of Philosophy and former President of [[Al-Quds University]].<ref>{{harvnb|Nusseibeh|2009|p=18}}.</ref> Another prominent descendant was [[Sadr al-Shari'a al-Asghar|Sadr al-Shari'a al-Thani]], a [[Hanafi]] scholar, and [[Maturidi]] philosophist.{{sfn|Nawhami|2017}}

'Ubadah influenced the Ansari descendants of later generations, who held elite positions in various areas, particularly [[Hejaz]].<ref name="The Religious Elite of the Early Islamic Ḥijāz Five Prosopographical Case Studies">{{cite book |last1=Ahmed |first1=Asad Q. |title=The Religious Elite of the Early Islamic Ḥijāz: Five Prosopographical Case Studies |date=2011 |publisher=Occasional Publications UPR |isbn=978-1-900934-13-8 |author2=Linacre College (University of Oxford). Unit for Prosopographical Research |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v1dwdBDDjcUC |language=en |series=Volume 14 of Occasional publications of the Oxford Unit for Prosopographical Research}}</ref>

Regarding 'Ubadah legacy of [[emancipation]], [[Mustafa al-Siba'i]] noted that emancipation within Islam was apparent due to the fact that there were one thousand (1,000) [[Dark skin|black skinned]] warriors under his command.{{sfn|al-Ghazali|2009|}} 'Ubadah rebuked the [[Discrimination based on skin color#Africa|racist]] attitude shown by scared, yet scornful Muqawqis towards [[black people]]s during the negotiation of the latter's surrender during the conquest of Egypt.{{sfn|Pipes|1980|p=4-5}}

'Ubadah ibn al-Samit (Arabic: عُبَادَة بۡن ٱلصَّامِت ʿUbādah ibn aṣ-Ṣāmit) was a companion of Muhammad and a well-respected chieftain of the Ansar. He participated in almost every battle during Muhammad's era. His official title, according to Muslim scholarly tradition, was 'Ubadah ibn Saamit al-Ansari al-Badri (عُبَادَة بۡن ٱلصَّامِت ٱلۡأَنْصَارِيّ ٱلۡبَدْرِيّ) for his actions at the Battle of Badr. He served under the first three Rashidun caliphs in the Muslim campaigns against the Byzantine Empire.

The conquest of Cyprus marked 'Ubadah as one of the Rashidun army's most successful military commanders.
